title: Free trial length: why longer trials convert but shorter ones buy attribution (Cal AI)
summary: Jake Castillo explains how to choose free trial length and whether to go freemium. Longer trials convert better because people forget to cancel, but shorter trials give clean install-to-revenue attribution when buying traffic through creators. Freemium only works when the free feature differs from the paid upsells.

principles.text: Run free trials only after proof of PMF; trials can't fix a boring product or bad messaging.
principles.quote: Free trials can be a part of any consumer app growth strategy, but only after you have significant proof that people actually want your product and will pay for it.

principles.text: Longer trials convert better because users forget to cancel, which also helps recoup ad spend.
principles.quote: So yes, longer trials convert better because you’re banking on subscribers forgetting to cancel.

principles.text: Short trials trigger immediate cancellations; most 3-day cancels happen on day 0 or 1.
principles.quote: According to RevenueCat, 84% of 3-day trial cancellations happen on day 0 or day 1.

principles.text: Every extra trial day adds noise between install and charge, hurting creator attribution.
principles.quote: Every day you add to your trial is another day of variables between the install and when their credit card gets charged.

principles.text: Attribution matters more than conversion rate when deciding which creators to keep, since audiences differ in paying power.
principles.quote: attribution is how you decide who to keep or cut on your roster of creators.

principles.text: Not paying for traffic: go long. Buying installs: shorten, since trial length is the price of signal.
principles.quote: You're not optimizing conversion at that point, you're buying signal, and trial length is what you pay for it.
